findings.reason: as written, the repair lets the live foreign worker through on the very record shape §14's run actually left behind (a retired `attempt-1-worker.json` with no exit beside it), so the node would ship a guard that still admits the double launch it was written for.
findings.text: §15 frees an off-host refusal on "the newest attempt's exit receipt" and names `_retired_attempt_ended` as the mechanism, but that helper (`reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:2083`) has no launching-host gate: with no exit receipt it answers by probing the worker receipt's pid against the *local* process table, so a foreign worker's pid reads dead here and the attempt reads as ended — reproducing exactly the "I cannot see this worker from here, therefore there is no worker" inversion §15 exists to fix, one layer deeper. `_worker_record_liveness` does gate on this (`recovery_liveness.py:308-309`, returning None for a known-foreign record); `_retired_attempt_ended` does not.

findings.reason: a node writing the fixture from this text cannot make both cases green without inventing the rule that separates them, and whichever rule it invents decides whether case (a) tests the refusal or tests nothing.
findings.text: §15's case (a) ("with a worker record and no exit receipt, is refused") and case (b) ("the same record with an exit receipt for its newest attempt proceeds") are unambiguous only if both use the same record shape, and they cannot: with a *canonical* `worker.json` present, `_launch_refused_by` never consults a receipt at all (`retired` is computed only when `WORKER_RECORD_NAME` is absent, `dispatch_launch.py:2149-2153`) and `_worker_record_liveness` returns None for a known-foreign record, so case (b) refuses; with *retired* `attempt-N-*` receipts, case (a) proceeds for the reason above. The section must state which shape decides and cover both.

findings.reason: the node either fails its own case (a) assertion or must change the message composer or the reading's payload, which the section says it will not — a deviation a build node would have to make silently or block on.
findings.text: §15 scopes the change to "the refusal predicate" and says the off-host answer in `live_worker_reading` is kept, but its done-when requires the refusal to name "the launching host and the recorded pid": `_live_worker_refusal(run_id, reading, consequence)` (`dispatch_launch.py:2044`) and `_live_worker_naming(reading)` (`:2020`) receive only a `LivenessReading`, which carries no host field (`process_liveness.py:326-341`) and whose off-host value is `LivenessReading(LIVENESS_UNKNOWN, None)` with `pid=None` (`recovery_liveness.py:1363`). A predicate returning a bool cannot supply either token.

findings.reason: the dispatch fence and the `changed_paths` audit are derived from the section's write paths; without them the node is unfenceable and its ruff-by-delta measure has no population.
findings.text: §15 declares no write paths and no gate-log location, while §5 through §13 each end with "Write paths: …" and "Every log under the run directory starts with its revision and the literal command and ends in a bare `EXIT=` line". Its done-when nonetheless refers to "the staged paths" for the ruff delta, so the text assumes a scope it never states.
